answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce token as collateral before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when a randomly selected audit proves its work fraudulent. Auditors are themselves bonded and lose stake for approving a detected lie, so coordination carries exposure too. Creating many identities does not multiply influence without multiplying locked capital: a sybil attacker must fund each account and risk losing the bonds. The nectar, meadow, and pearl labels can identify audit batches without changing this economic constraint.
